# QLogic ISP12160 dual-channel Ultra3 SCSI host adapter (PCI 1077:1216), the constants the held sources establish

The two-channel QLogic SCSI host adapter on the Origin 300 IO-8 board and the Origin 350 IO9 board (PCI 1077:1216). Grades say how each item was derived: established means a vendor datasheet, a hardware capture or a driver or firmware statement that names the value directly; inferred means a software expectation, a shipped program that uses the value and does not show the chip's own behaviour, or a reading of a value's meaning from one driver's use of it. No register offsets, reset values or mailbox operand layouts beyond those named here are held for this part, so the register map is not in this unit. The mailbox opcodes are the values the shipped programs send, not measured chip behaviour.

Unit `isp12160`, macro prefix `ISP12160`.
Default source: QLogic ISP12160A data sheet (1999); QLogic QLA12160 hardware installation guide (2001); IRIX 6.5 Bedrock-class controller object; IRIX 6.5 Octane SCSI driver object; Linux qla1280, NetBSD isp and OpenBSD qlw drivers (pins in references/documents/INDEX.md); stock PROM 6.210 SCSI diagnostic.

Every item has a grade: established, inferred or unknown. A grade says how the item was derived from its source; it does not claim the item was measured on silicon.

## Constants

| Constant | Value | Grade | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BUSES` | 0x2 | established | QLogic ISP12160A data sheet (1999), first page: dual-channel Ultra3 SCSI; IRIX 6.5 Octane SCSI driver object sends per-bus commands for a part with more than one bus | SCSI channels per chip. The ISP1040 has one; this part has two, each a separate SCSI bus with its own selection timeout, reset delay and target state. |
| `BUS_RESET_DELAY_DEFAULT_S` | 0x5 | established | QLogic ISP12160A data sheet (1999); QLogic QLA12160 hardware installation guide (2001); IRIX 6.5 Bedrock-class controller object; IRIX 6.5 Octane SCSI driver object; Linux qla1280, NetBSD isp and OpenBSD qlw drivers (pins in references/documents/INDEX.md); stock PROM 6.210 SCSI diagnostic | Default SCSI bus reset delay in seconds, per bus, in the Fast!UTIL NVRAM setting of the QLA12160 board. The guide says that after a bus reset the firmware starts no SCSI activity for the set number of seconds. That is an established statement about the setting. Whether the 0x0018 mailbox value starts the same hold-off is inferred (see OP_BUS_RESET). |
| `BUS_RESET_DELAY_MAX_S` | 0xf | established | QLogic ISP12160A data sheet (1999); QLogic QLA12160 hardware installation guide (2001); IRIX 6.5 Bedrock-class controller object; IRIX 6.5 Octane SCSI driver object; Linux qla1280, NetBSD isp and OpenBSD qlw drivers (pins in references/documents/INDEX.md); stock PROM 6.210 SCSI diagnostic | Largest SCSI bus reset delay the Fast!UTIL setting accepts, in seconds, per bus. |
| `CONTROLLER_PROGRAM_WORDS` | 0x361d | inferred | IRIX 6.5 Bedrock-class controller object: the separate ISP12160 controller program it carries is 27,706 bytes, and the program's image header word at index 3 is this value | Length in 16-bit words of the controller program the IRIX 6.5 Bedrock-class object downloads to this part, read from zero-based image word 3. The value is the length of one shipped program. It is a software expectation, not a chip fact, and says nothing about the RAM the chip has. |
| `DRIVER_SELECTION_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT` | 0xfa | inferred | IRIX 6.5 Octane SCSI driver object: per-bus record defaults for device 0x1216 | Selection timeout the Octane driver stores in its per-bus record and then programs with the selection-timeout command. It is the driver's own default, not a chip default. |
| `OP_ABORT_DEVICE` | 0x16 | inferred | IRIX 6.5 Bedrock-class controller object, which constructs this request and calls the recovery helper that issues it; the Linux qla1280 driver header names the same opcode | Abort device: abort the outstanding requests for one LUN on one target of one channel. Mailbox 1 packs the channel in bit 15, the target in bits 14:8 and the LUN in bits 7:0. Mailboxes 2 and 3 are zero. The object does not expose a request handle, so this command takes the packed selector and no handle. It is separate from the command abort and target reset opcodes. |
| `OP_BUS_RESET` | 0x18 | inferred | IRIX 6.5 Bedrock-class controller object (the request it builds); mailbox placement matches Linux qla1280's bus reset (driver header and bus-reset routine) (see the ISP1040 unit's OP_BUS_RESET) | Reset one SCSI channel. Mailbox 1 carries a byte the request builder reads from that channel's state, which the object does not name or give units for. Mailbox 2 carries the channel number. The delay's meaning is inferred from the ISP1040 unit's reading (seconds, starting a hold-off on the bus), and the 6.5 Octane driver object sends the same command once per bus with the delay in mailbox 1 and the bus number in mailbox 2. Whether the firmware refuses or holds commands for that hold-off, and whether it posts an asynchronous reset event for a reset the host requested, are unknown. |
| `OP_DUMP_RAM` | 0x3 | inferred | stock PROM 6.210 SCSI diagnostic, which prepares this opcode against the ISP12160 when it tests DMA | Dump RAM: the controller returns its RAM to the host. The pair of the load opcode above. The mailbox operand layout is not given here. |
| `OP_LOAD_RAM` | 0x1 | inferred | stock PROM 6.210 SCSI diagnostic, which prepares this opcode against the ISP12160 when it tests DMA | Load RAM: the host writes controller RAM. The mailbox operand layout is not given here. The opcode and its direction are software expectations from the diagnostic that sends it, not a chip datasheet statement. |
| `OP_SET_SELECTION_TIMEOUT` | 0x31 | inferred | Linux qla1280 (its driver header and controller set-up code, a driver for the QLA12160 as well), and the NetBSD isp and OpenBSD qlw drivers; IRIX 6.5 Octane SCSI driver object for device 0x1216 | Set the selection timeout. Mailbox 1 is bus 0's value and mailbox 2 is bus 1's, as the three public drivers write them and the Octane driver writes them for this device. Unit inferred to be milliseconds, as for the ISP1040, with a driver default of 250. The chip's own default when never programmed is unknown. |
| `PCI_BUS_WIDTH_BITS` | 0x40 | established | QLogic ISP12160A data sheet (1999), first page: "64-bit bus master" | Width of the PCI host interface, and so of the data phases the part runs as a bus master, per the data sheet. Whether the board wires the 64-bit lines on each slot or bus is a separate question and is not settled here. |
| `PCI_CLOCK_MHZ` | 0x42 | established | QLogic ISP12160A data sheet (1999), first page: "66-MHz, 64-bit PCI host bus interface" (the /66 version; a /33 version also exists) | PCI clock the data sheet gives for the host interface. The data sheet's own claim; no capture or driver states the clock the board runs. |
| `PCI_DEVICE_ID` | 0x1216 | established | QLogic ISP12160A data sheet (1999); QLogic QLA12160 hardware installation guide (2001); IRIX 6.5 Bedrock-class controller object; IRIX 6.5 Octane SCSI driver object; Linux qla1280, NetBSD isp and OpenBSD qlw drivers (pins in references/documents/INDEX.md); stock PROM 6.210 SCSI diagnostic | PCI device ID of the ISP12160 under vendor 0x1077.
